name: heavy-loss
description: Protocol-selective loss: 30% of TCP packets are dropped at random in each direction; UDP is untouched. TCP connections open (eventually) and then crawl — no TCP-based family can move the probe's payload within its budget. The QUIC families are unaffected. Which step a TCP family fails at differs from run to run, so no failure category is asserted — but each must still be shown to have connected and authenticated (family/established: one nonce through the tunnel and back, retried for up to 60 s), or a dead family would read as a slow one.
analogue: Iran's protest-period shaping: 'protocol-selective shaping degrades HTTPS handshake completion below 50%' (OONI/M-Lab), and the ~40% packet loss measured at the TIC chokepoint in March-April 2024. Model: independent per-packet random drop of TCP only. The real shaping is bursty, rate-based and keyed on more than the protocol number; and where it also hits UDP the QUIC families would suffer too (measured here with 30% loss on everything: hysteria2 and tuic still completed the fetch, in 7-11 s instead of 40 ms).

nft: meta l4proto tcp numgen random mod 100 < 30 drop
